definitions.gloss: chief priest of a Shinto shrine
definitions.explanation: The highest-ranking priest who oversees the administration and rituals of a Shinto shrine. Each shrine typically has one chief priest.

examples.japanese: {宮司|ぐうじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{祝詞|のりと}→祝詞：30669_norito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}み{上|あ}げた→読み上げる：04604_yomiageru⟧。
examples.english: The chief priest read out the Shinto prayer.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{宮司|ぐうじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{代々|だいだい}→代々：05899_daidai⟧⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧⟦{家系|かけい}→家系：10130_kakei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{務|つと}めている→務める：10446_tsutomeru⟧。
examples.english: The chief priest of this shrine has been served by the same family for generations.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新年|しんねん}→新年：09787_shinnen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{祭事|さいじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}けて→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧、{宮司|ぐうじ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{進|すす}めている→進める：01949_susumeru⟧。
examples.english: The chief priest is making preparations for the New Year festivities.

notes:
USAGE:
{宮司|ぐうじ} is specific to Shinto shrines. The equivalent for a Buddhist temple would be ⟦{住職|じゅうしょく}→住職：15520_juushoku⟧ (head priest). Below the {宮司|ぐうじ} in the shrine hierarchy are ⟦{禰宜|ねぎ}→禰宜：24980_negi⟧ (senior priest) and {権禰宜|ごんねぎ} (junior priest).

The word combines {宮|ぐう} (shrine/palace) and {司|じ} (to manage/oversee).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {宮司|ぐうじ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{務|つと}める→務める：10446_tsutomeru⟧: to serve as chief priest
- {宮司|ぐうじ}⟦{職|しょく}→職：00376_shoku⟧: the position of chief priest
- ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{宮司|ぐうじ}: chief priest of a shrine
